latest.title: Beyond Transformers: Tesseract-Based Quantum-Inspired Neural Architectures
latest.summary: This manuscript proposes a comprehensive framework for quantum-inspired neural architectures grounded in Tesseract-based mathematical structures. The work introduces novel approaches to high-dimensional neural computation, quantum state representation, and cross-dimensional information processing. We demonstrate how 4D/5D topological structures can enhance neural network expressiveness, enable more efficient representation of complex patterns, and provide new pathways for superintelligence research. The architecture integrates dimensional binding, lattice-based error correction, and hierarchical feature extraction within a unified quantum-inspired computational paradigm.

items.summary: Machine-learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs) have shown significant promise in predicting infrared spectra with high fidelity. items.title: Cercospora Diseases: Advances in Epidemiology, Host Pathogen Interaction and Sustainable Management Strategies
items.summary: Cercospora is a widespread and destructive genus of fungi that causes leaf spot diseases on many economically important crops, including pulses, cereals, oilseeds, and vegetables. Global crop losses from these pathogens typically range between 50% and 75%. This review brings together evidence on taxonomy, diversity, morphology, host range, epidemiology, host–pathogen interactions and management options. Morphological characteristics, including septate mycelium, conidiophore arrangement and conidial form, vary among species. The genus exhibits substantial morphological and ecological diversity and molecular studies have shown that its host association ranges from strict specialization to…

items.title: Laboratory records of line-to-line and three-phase faults at a 60 kVA grid-following converter behind a Dy11 transformer
items.summary: 39 records (10 kHz, 10 s each) of a 60 kVA grid-following converter connected to a grid emulator through a 70 kVA Dy11 transformer: 24 line-to-line faults, 13 three-phase faults and 2 records without fault, applied with a fault emulator at the grid-side bus. Voltages are recorded at the grid-side measurement box and at the converter terminals. The records are the laboratory validation data of the paper "Understanding the Geometry of Faulted Power Systems under High Penetration of Inverter-Based Resources via Ellipse Fitting and Geometric Algebra" (arXiv:2509.10044). See README.md for the variables, the order of the channels and the notes for the user.

items.title: Intrinsic Two-Diameter Wave Geometry on the Punctured Euler–Clifford Plane: Wave-Defined Oblique Channels, Geometric Pauli Blockade, and Standing-Wave Nano-Transistors on Carbon-Nanotube Walls
items.summary: Smooth continuum derivatives (Δx → 0, Δt → 0), radial coordinates anchored inside point origins, and idempotent set operations ({a,a} = {a}) obscure discrete cycle counting and state conservation at the scale of individual Planck action quanta h. items.title: Real-time neuromorphic audio and vision perception for autonomous robotic applications: Integration and experimental evaluation on a rover platform
items.summary: Neuromorphic sensing and computing offer a promising alternative to conventional deep learning pipelines for mobile robots, where perception must run continuously under tight latency and energy constraints. However, most neuromorphic solutions are still evaluated offline or on isolated benchmarks, and their integration into complete robotic systems remains largely unexplored. In this technical report, a four-wheel rover platform is presented that combines three real-time perception pipelines: a classical audio tagging pipeline based on Pretrained Audio Neural Networks (PANNs) running on an NVIDIA Jetson GPU, a neuromorphic audio pipeline in which a spiking neural network (SNN) is deployed…

items.title: BioEmu2: Scalable Emulation of Biomolecular Dynamics
items.summary: Despite major advances in structure prediction, modelling the motions and interactions that drive biomolecular function at scale remains a central challenge. We introduce BioEmu2, a generative model for atomically resolved biomolecular structures combining static structure prediction, equilibrium sampling and time evolution, that samples orders of magnitude faster than molecular dynamics (MD). Trained on experimental and synthetic structures and extensive MD data, it supports multi-component systems containing proteins, nucleic acids, modified residues, ligands and ions. Structure-prediction accuracy is comparable to top open-weight biomolecular folding models, and a context parallel mode…

items.title: Interpretable Tissue Architecture Complements Pathology Foundation Models
items.summary: Tissue architecture provides important information for histopathological assessment, yet its complementary predictive value alongside pathology foundation-model representations remains insufficiently understood. This study investigates whether interpretable measurements of cellular and multicellular tissue organization provide additional predictive information beyond learned representations. We introduce a 139-dimensional cellular-to-community representation comprising nine feature groups characterizing nuclear morphology, cellular composition, spatial connectivity, community organization, and cell-cell interactions. Their predictive contributions are systematically evaluated independently…

items.title: LesionAgent: Training-Free Agentic Tumor Tracking and Response Assessment in Longitudinal CT
items.summary: Every few months, a cancer patient's CT scans decide whether treatment continues. 3D foundation models can now detect, segment, register and track lesions, yet none of them reads the scans as a radiologist does. A radiologist decides which findings are lesions, which are the same lesion months later and whether a new spot means progression, and checks each decision against the extensive rules of a clinical guideline. We introduce LesionAgent, an LLM agent that performs this read end to end without task-specific training. It operates frozen 3D models as tools, acts in 3D through coordinate-labelled views, remembers every lesion across visits in a registry, verifies every model output it…

items.title: Magnetic-Field Response of a Hyperbolic Kitaev Spin Liquid
items.summary: Hyperbolic geometry can give rise to Kitaev spin liquids with distinct flux structures and Majorana spectra, raising the question of how these fractionalized states respond beyond exactly solvable limits. We address this question on the Kekulé-colored hyperbolic {8,3} lattice by developing an infinite projected entangled-pair-state approach with flux-resolved loop-gas initialization and geometry-adapted tensor-network contraction. Under uniform and staggered [111] magnetic fields, we find markedly different many-body responses. The uniform field induces a sharp change between competing variational branches at weak field, whereas the polarization and mean plaquette flux evolve over a much…

items.title: Neural Defend ARCAS 290M: A Robust Foundation Model for AI-Generated Audio Detection
items.summary: Voice cloning now needs only seconds of audio, and detectors tuned to one dataset often fail when the generator, channel, or language changes. We introduce ARCAS 290M, Neural Defend's foundation model for detecting AI-generated audio. A single frozen production model, with no benchmark-specific fine-tuning, generalizes across text-to-speech, voice-conversion, and codec-language-model generators, telephone and Bluetooth channels, recording conditions, and languages. We evaluate it on the complete official test sets of ten public benchmarks, scoring every recording exactly as released, and against commercial systems on independent leaderboards. ARCAS 290M ranks first among all systems on the…

items.title: Search-RSI: Expanding Search Worlds Along Multimodal Agents' Capability Frontier
items.summary: Multimodal search agents answer knowledge intensive visual questions by grounding them in retrieved evidence, and recent recipes train them on multi hop tasks that are synthesized from knowledge graphs and grown online to keep pace with the agent. These recipes, however, treat the searchable world as fixed: a new question can be well formed and verifiable while its evidence is absent from the retrieval backend, so the agent issues the right query, retrieves nothing, and is penalized as if its policy were at fault. Such unreachable negatives accumulate with every round of growth. We propose Search-RSI, a recursive self improvement framework that expands the search world along the agent's…

items.title: AutoOntologyBench: A Task-Grounded Benchmark for Agentic Knowledge Engineering
items.summary: Foundation-model agents are increasingly extending beyond software engineering (SWE) into autonomous scientific research, where acquiring and integrating domain knowledge remains a critical challenge. Recent industrial advances have increasingly adopted knowledge graphs and ontology-based semantic layers to organize heterogeneous knowledge into reusable representations. We ask: Can autonomous agents construct ontologies that help them solve real tasks, and do they offer measurable benefits over alternative knowledge representations? Existing benchmarks evaluate ontology correctness or agent task success in isolation, leaving the value of autonomously acquired knowledge unresolved. We…

items.title: Do Alice and Bob Dream of the Oracle? Wishful Cryptanalysis
items.summary: For two millennia, offense and defense have forged cryptographic security boundaries. Tools automated calculation and search, while humans drove discovery. Foundation models now mark a shift from automated computation to intelligent scientific discovery. Because cryptanalysis rests on exact mathematical definitions and immediately executable truth, it offers a proving ground for autonomous intelligence to move past security reliant on scarce human attention and explore structures beyond human working memory. Unguided models stall between two opposite traps: authority hallucination, where they surrender whenever prior literature declares a route blocked, and reasoning hallucination, where…

items.title: Embodied-Harness: Towards Recursive Self-Improvement for Robotic Manipulation
items.summary: Vision-language model (VLM)-based agents offer a promising approach to robotic manipulation, yet remain limited by inadequate memory organization, uncertain failure attribution, and limited reuse of execution experience. We propose Embodied-Harness, a dual-agent framework that improves manipulation by refining the execution harness without updating model parameters. The Actor interacts with the environment through a robot-control interface, while the Reflector converts execution evidence into reusable operational guidance. Hierarchical Memory Architecture maintains short-term execution context and long-term experiential knowledge to support execution and reflection. Evidence-based…

items.title: Learning in Symbiosis: Heterogeneous Federated Learning with ANNs and SNNs
items.summary: Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs), widely regarded as the third generation of neural networks, represent a promising neuromorphic computing paradigm with the potential to reduce the energy footprint of Artificial Intelligence (AI). Their en-ergy efficiency makes SNNs particularly attractive for resource-constrained Edge AI devices, motivating growing research interest in Federated Learning (FL) with SNNs. Despite these advantages, integrating SNNs into existing FL systems remains challenging, as replacing all conventional Artificial Neural Network (ANN) devices with SNN-based alternatives is impractical. Instead, we envision a gradual transition toward neuromorphic Edge AI, where ANN and SNN…

items.title: Adapting AI Weather Foundation Models to a Changing Climate
items.summary: AI weather foundation models learn from historical archives, while the climate distribution encountered during deployment continues to evolve. This growing model--climate mismatch motivates continual adaptation without repeated full-model retraining, but the structure of weather forecast errors determines how such adaptation should be performed. We develop an online adaptation framework that exploits two complementary error structures: geographically persistent biases and flow-dependent errors that vary with the atmospheric state. Analysis of Aurora-1.3B reveals strongly concentrated forecast-loss sensitivity in its decoder, motivating flow-dependent corrections within fixed…

items.title: S-BFM: A Behavioral Foundation Model for Humanoid Control from Sparse Spatiotemporal Goals
items.summary: General-purpose whole-body trackers can execute diverse humanoid motions, but they require dense reference trajectories. However, tasks usually specify only where, in which posture, and when the robot should arrive, leaving the motion in between to a separate planner. Inspired by human motor coordination, our key idea is that a low-level controller can organize the intervening motion and its pace by itself from sparse goals with arrival times. In this paper, we propose S-BFM, a novel behavioral foundation model superior in its autonomy: it generates whole-body transitions from target postures, poses, and arrival times alone. Specifically, we first introduce Spatial Grounding, which adds…

items.title: From Tokens to Pixels: Training-Free Guided Upsampling of Frozen CARL Features for Hyperspectral Imaging
items.summary: Camera-agnostic foundation models such as CARL map spectral images from arbitrary sensors into a shared feature space, but deliver their features only on a token grid at one eighth of the input resolution. The usual bilinear interpolation blurs material boundaries over about one token and rounds off corners. We investigate how much spatial accuracy image-guided upsampling recovers for frozen CARL features without training the encoder or the upsampler. We compare joint bilateral upsampling (JBU), a guided filter and the pretrained AnyUp, each with the hyperspectral image or an RGB rendering as the guide. A hyperspectral ColorChecker dataset acquired specifically for this study, with…

items.title: EchoAlign: Echocardiography foundation model with multilevel report alignment
items.summary: Echocardiography assesses the structure and function of the heart. Cardiologists read each study across several standard views and report the findings visible in those views by cardiac structure. AI foundation models can learn to analyze these studies from clinical reports, reducing annotation burden and supporting clinical interpretation. However, existing models are trained by pairing each video with the full clinical report, including structures and findings its view does not show. This mismatch lets a model associate a finding with incidental or spurious signals rather than its visual evidence, which limits accuracy, anatomical grounding and clinical trust. Here we introduce EchoAlign,…

items.title: NavRSI: Recursive Harness Self-Improvement for Vision-and-Language Navigation
items.summary: Frontier large language models (LLMs) have enabled vision-and-language navigation (VLN) through direct closed-loop perception and action. However, navigation performance depends strongly on the harness governing LLM-environment interactions, while existing harnesses largely rely on manually designed navigation tools, memory, and agent roles. We introduce NavRSI, a harness-centric recursive self-improvement framework that optimizes the navigation behavior of frozen LLMs through closed-loop experience. In each round, NavRSI iteratively collects navigation trajectories and failure diagnostics, employs a designer agent to rewrite the harness, and retains the revisions that prove effective,…

items.title: On the Challenges of Using LLMs in High-Risk AI Recruitment: Guiding Questions for Legal Conformity with the AI Act
items.summary: The EU Artificial Intelligence Act (AI Act) imposes detailed obligations on providers of high-risk AI systems but offers limited operational guidance, particularly when these systems integrate third-party General-Purpose AI (GPAI) models. This paper introduces a toolkit that fosters the development of legal-by-design AI-assisted recruitment systems by translating the core legal obligations of the AI Act's conformity assessment---specifically Articles 9--15 and Annex IV---into techno-normative requirements and corresponding guiding questions. While recruitment pipelines may involve components with varying technical complexity and differing levels of algorithmic transparency, this paper…

items.title: Taking Apart and Putting Together: Tracking Objects Through Physical Transformations
items.summary: We introduce Transformation Tracking and Understanding (TTU), extending video object tracking to environments where objects undergo physical assemblies and disassemblies. TTU requires continuously tracking objects through transformations, identifying new entities, maintaining a state graph of their relationships, and assigning semantic labels to transformations. While foundation models (e.g., SAM 2/3) maintain tracklets through appearance changes, they cannot update semantic identities as objects physically evolve. Prior work addresses only disassemblies, relying on expensive searches triggered only when tracking fails. We propose Tracking Instances via Proposals and Overlaps (TIPO), a…

items.title: Regularizing gravity in the presence of matter fields
items.summary: We investigate how matter fields affect spacetime regularity in a class of gravitational theories with second-order field equations in spherical symmetry, of which general relativity is a special case, and which may encode effective corrections from an underlying quantum theory of gravity. Focusing on spherically symmetric black holes and cosmological spacetimes in theories in which vacuum spacetimes display bounded curvature invariants, we derive the conditions under which regular geometries can be supported by static and perturbative scalar fields, electromagnetic fields, and radiation fluids. We discuss the impact of matter on the regularity requirements of curvature boundedness and…

items.title: Latent Jacobian Steer: Eliciting Contact-Rich Out-of-Distribution Behaviors from Pretrained Humanoid Controllers
items.summary: Given a pretrained general latent-conditioned whole-body humanoid controller, say a behavioral foundation model (BFM), how can we elicit complex and contact-rich out-of-distribution behaviors? Raw joint-action exploration enables direct, task-specific adjustments but can disrupt coordination learned by the pretrained controller, whereas latent exploration retains that coordination but is difficult to steer toward desired physical effects. To combine the complementary strengths of these exploration spaces, we propose Latent Jacobian Steer (LJS), which couples sampling in direct joint-action space with the semantics of the learned frozen controller's input latent space. For a task specified…

items.title: 60-cm-long In-vacuum Zerodur Optical Cavity for Optical Lattice Atom Interferometry
items.summary: Optical cavities are widely used in atomic physics experiments to control the spatial geometry and spectral properties of atom-light interactions. Recently, an optical lattice generated by the pristine mode of an optical cavity was utilized to hold and extend the quantum coherence of atomic spatial superpositions. Here, we describe an in-vacuum optical cavity designed to enhance the spatial and temporal coherence of optical lattice atom interferometers to one millimeter wavepacket separations and one minute measurement durations. The cavity uses a rigid Zerodur spacer to suppress the negative effects of thermal drift and mechanical-acoustic vibrations on the atomic motional state. The 60…

items.title: Spiking Neural Networks Incrementally Track Firing-Rate Networks
items.summary: Understanding how spiking neural networks (SNNs) efficiently process data streams is key to (i) studying how biological brains conserve energy for lifelong predictions and (ii) enabling efficient continuous AI inference. In this work, we propose a theory on how an SNN incrementally tracks its corresponding firing-rate network, a continuous-valued neural network (ANN). We prove that the output of a discrete SNN continuously tracks the instantaneous ANN output implicitly determined by the SNN input. Based on this principle, we develop LIF-Stream, a conversion framework for efficient SNN inference over unbounded data streams. It enables the converted SNN to reuse its prior activation state…

items.title: InterBand-EMG: A Cross-Band Foundation Model for Generalizable Hand-Pose Estimation
items.summary: Surface electromyography (sEMG) enables continuous hand-pose estimation, but learning representations that generalize across users and movements remains challenging. We introduce InterBand-EMG, which combines band-specific quantization with cross-band reconstruction and structured masked code prediction to learn transferable EMG representations for hand-pose tracking. We also introduce SynapMyo, an eight-channel EMG-to-pose dataset comprising 1,227.74 hand-hours from 499 users across 68 movement categories. Experiments on emg2pose and SynapMyo show that InterBand-EMG outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in joint-angle accuracy across all three generalization settings on both datasets.…

items.title: SIR-Agent: Skill-Augmented Image Restoration Agent with Recursive Self-Improvement
items.summary: Agents for Image Restoration (IR) aim to leverage Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) to autonomously perceive image degradation and invoke IR tools. However, existing IR agents typically rely on fine-tuning MLLM parameters to adapt to new IR tasks, leading to catastrophic forgetting of IR knowledge. To address this limitation, we propose a skill-augmented IR agent, dubbed SIR-Agent, that maintains IR knowledge in a scalable skill library and uses Recursive Self-Improvement (RSI) to facilitate efficient skill-library evolution. Specifically, we design a Chain Feedback-driven Skill Revision (CFSR) to evolve the skill library. The CFSR analyzes restoration chains to identify and revise…

items.title: Stratum: A Hardware-Software Co-Design Framework for SNN Inference on RISC-V
items.summary: Efficient spiking neural network (SNN) inference on RISC-V processors requires tracing implementation costs back to the compiler and hardware decisions that produce them. Training environments, compilers, and cycle-level simulators, however, typically operate as distinct tools, making this attribution difficult. This paper presents Stratum, a framework that integrates an snnTorch-trained SNN, an MLIR-based compiler stack, and a cycle-level gem5-based RISC-V model into a unified workflow. Stratum exposes two optimization levers, software decisions in the generated code and hardware configuration choices in the simulated core, and uses stage-level cycle measurements to identify performance…

items.title: Dark Energy Based on Modified Gravity: Where the Future Lies?
items.summary: Based on current observational data, there is a strong possibility that dark energy was in a phantom regime in the near past, and a transition from a phantom to a quintessential regime may have occurred. Since then, many scenarios compatible with the DESI data have been proposed. In particular, there exist several realistic models in the framework of $F(R)$ gravity. In this paper, we show that such realistic models of $F(R)$ gravity may produce an anti-gravity or ghost graviton in the future. The problem could be avoided by further changing the parameters and fine-tuning the initial conditions, but we propose to introduce a potential barrier of the scalar field for the small scalar…

items.title: ECG-LabWAS: A Laboratory-Wide Association Study Using a Fine-Tuned Single-Lead Electrocardiogram Foundation Model
items.summary: Laboratory testing guides clinical diagnosis but requires blood sampling and processing. The electrocardiogram (ECG) is fast and noninvasive and may carry information about laboratory abnormalities, yet most AI-ECG models target one test at a time using 12-lead recordings. We conducted an exploratory ECG laboratory-wide association study (ECG-LabWAS), fine-tuning an ECG foundation model pretrained on 10.8 million ECGs to screen 50 laboratory tests from single-lead waveforms alone. The model was developed in an emergency-department cohort (MC-MED; 31,826 patients) and applied unchanged to an independent hospital cohort (MIMIC-IV; 115,921 patients). Of 89 abnormality directions (low or high…

items.title: Neural Defend Ranks #1 in Global Audio Deepfake Detection Benchmark - ARCAS on the Podonos Independent Leaderboard
items.summary: Commercial detectors of AI-generated audio are usually promoted with results on internal test sets that buyers cannot inspect. Independent benchmarks with private labels give a more reliable comparison. We report the results of Neural Defend's ARCAS foundation models on the Podonos audio deepfake detection benchmark, an independent leaderboard that scores commercial detection APIs and open-source detectors on one held-out set of real speech and speech from current text-to-speech and voice-cloning systems, delivered in six file formats, against labels that only Podonos holds. In the release of 29 October 2026, which covers 28 systems from 16 commercial vendors and the leading open models,…

items.title: A Frugal AI Framework for India: Responsible and Right-sized AI
items.summary: India's AI debate often swings between two insufficient options: replicating the compute-intensive, capital-heavy foundation-model programmes of the United States or China, or remaining a downstream adopter of foreign AI with localised interfaces and safeguards. Neither serves a country that must deliver AI to a very large, diverse population across uneven infrastructure and within constrained budgets. This white paper from the Centre for Responsible AI (CeRAI), IIT Madras, proposes a third path: Responsible Frugal AI, which applies principle-based frugal engineering alongside Responsible AI. Responsible Frugal AI is right-sized AI: it fixes the functional requirement first, asks whether…

items.title: BusemannFormer: Horospherical Self-Attention for Hyperbolic Graph Transformers
items.summary: Hyperbolic neural networks excel on hierarchical graph data, yet existing hyperbolic Transformers largely adapt conventional attention without explicitly exploiting the ideal boundary, a geometric structure closely tied to tree hierarchy. We propose Horospherical Self-Attention (HSA): each query selects an ideal-boundary direction and scores keys by their Busemann depth along that direction, yielding a token-to-token hyperbolic attention kernel. We establish a flat-limit connection to dot-product attention, characterize score level sets as horospheres, and bound key-side gradients. HSA is integrated into BusemannFormer, a fully hyperbolic graph Transformer, with a log-depth variant that…

items.title: FM4SAR-Bench 1.0: Towards A Fair Benchmark for Evaluating Foundation Models for SAR Image Interpretation
items.summary: Foundation models have advanced SAR image interpretation but created a heterogeneous, fragmented model ecosystem. Existing models differ substantially in their input, training data, objectives, architectures, and release policy, yet the field lacks a unified taxonomy and comparative framework. Current evaluations rely primarily on task-specific benchmarks, which are ill-suited to fair comparison among models with fundamentally different input-output formats and task paradigms, and often overlook data transparency, reproducibility, interpretability, and deployment readiness. Limited SAR data accessibility also means high reported performance does not guarantee access to training data, code,…

items.title: How Does SAM-3 Adapt? Capacity, Update Geometry, and Domain Transfer
items.summary: Promptable segmentation foundation models are increasingly used in specialized domains, but it remains unclear how SAM-3 should be fine-tuned when adapting it beyond its original training distribution. We study this question by comparing five adaptation families --LoRA, HiRA, KRAdapter, QuanTA, and Full Fine-Tuning-- across five segmentation datasets spanning medical imaging, remote sensing, and dense material segmentation. Across these datasets, compact parameter-efficient fine-tuning methods often match or approach Full Fine-Tuning in DSC and IoU, suggesting that strong in-domain adaptation does not always require updating the full model. However, this performance cannot be explained by…

items.title: The $n!$ theorem via quaternionic rotation of Cherednik algebras
items.summary: We give a proof of the $n!$ theorem based on the representation theory of Cherednik algebras and an analog of the rotation of complex structures arising from an action of the quaternions.

items.title: One state, many questions: Opsis gives a frontier model typed eyes for pathology
items.summary: A synoptic pathology report is a checklist of questions with fixed answer sets, many composed from others. Pathology foundation models answer them accurately with one classifier trained with labels for each, and frontier language models, which compose freely, cannot fit a slide of fourteen thousand tiles in their context. On 189 breast report questions, frontier models that read a written description of the slide or look at a thumbnail and tiles of it answer at 0.50 to 0.66, below the majority class at 0.67. A description is written before the question is known, and a look covers a handful of tiles. We present Opsis, which lets the model ask instead: a typed question interface on a frozen…

items.summary: This preprint (TKQB02) examines the vulnerability of quantum-coherent states in neural microtubules under galactic cosmic radiation (GCR) and proposes neuroprotective molecular targets for deep-space missions. Building on TKQB01 (Quantum Neurolinguistics), it analyses how high-LET particles threaten three candidate mechanisms — π-electron delocalisation in aromatic residues, low-barrier proton tunnelling, and Fröhlich-type coherent oscillations — and ranks their expected fragility. Five falsifiable space-medicine hypotheses (S1–S5) and a three-gate ground-based experimental roadmap are presented, designed for existing heavy-ion facilities and neural organoid platforms. items.title: When measurements of AI systems disagree A methodological review of dissociations in AI safety
items.summary: Abstract Artificial intelligence safety research compares systems' answers and actions with output probabilities, generated reasoning, internal activations and monitoring judgments. These measurements can disagree about what a system knows, what influenced its response and whether unwanted behavior occurred. This critical tutorial review organizes the emerging literature around five comparisons: relative sensitivity, incremental value, functional dissociation, causal intervention and targeted robustness. Worked examples distinguish reported findings, their inferential limits and informative follow-up comparisons. The comparisons are introduced through simpler settings and then applied…

items.title: A multimodal foundation model for molecular and morphologic data in oncology.
items.summary: Foundation models are advancing computational pathology by transferring knowledge from large datasets to diagnostic, prognostic and treatment response tasks. Most existing models, however, either operate at the patch level or learn slide-level representations using image-based objectives, coarse tissue labels or pathology reports that vary across institutions and reflect the subjectivity inherent in narrative reporting. Here we introduce THREADS, which instead learns general-purpose whole-slide representations by aligning tissue morphology with genomic or transcriptomic profiles. THREADS was pretrained on over 47,000 hematoxylin-and-eosin-stained tissue sections and evaluated across 107…

items.title: Continual learning in oncology AI: A framework for safe clinical translation.
items.summary: AI models remain largely static, yet cancer care never stands still. Evolution of scanning technology, imaging protocols, staging criteria, therapies, and patient populations can silently erode model performance and patient safety. Continual learning (CL) enables models to continuously acquire new knowledge, while minimizing catastrophic forgetting. Here, we review CL methods and their oncology applications, predominantly in imaging and pathology, and discuss CL as an option for maintaining foundation models, alongside recalibration and retraining. We examine translational barriers, including hidden regressions in underrepresented populations, label and concept drift, privacy constraints…

items.title: Probing Kaniadakis Holographic Dark Energy in a Bianchi Type-V Self-Creation Universe: Dynamics and Diagnostics
items.summary: Abstract We study a spatially homogeneous and anisotropic Bianchi type-V universe in Barber’s second self-creation theory of gravitation, filled with pressureless dark matter and an anisotropic Kaniadakis holographic dark energy (KHDE) fluid with a Hubble-horizon cutoff. We show that the off-diagonal field equation forces the two skewness parameters of the dark-energy fluid to be equal and opposite, δ = −γ, so that a fluid with two equal principal pressures is necessarily isotropic. Moreover, the vanishing-trace condition often used to integrate the scalar-field equation is equivalent to a vanishing Ricci scalar and over-determines the system; instead, we integrate the scalar-field…

items.title: A new approach to fixed-time synchronization of spatiotemporal memristive neural networks with mixed time-varying delays.
items.summary: This paper addresses the fixed-time synchronization (FXTS) problems of spatiotemporal memristive neural networks with mixed delays and reaction-diffusion terms (MDRDMNNs) via aperiodically semi-intermittent switching control (ASISC). First, a novel fixed-time stability criterion based on the hyperbolic-cosine function is established, and an explicit upper bound estimation of the settling time is derived, thereby providing a new theoretical perspective for achieving system synchronization. Furthermore, leveraging the established fixed-time stability results and introducing the ASISC strategy, which exhibits distinct advantages in energy efficiency and cost reduction over continuous control,…

items.title: Brain-inspired low-rank spiking neural networks for aircraft control with manifold representation reinforcement learning.
items.summary: Achieving stable and rapid aircraft attitude control under flight uncertainty and external disturbance remains a challenging task. To address this problem, this paper proposes a manifold representation reinforcement learning framework based on a Low-rank recurrent spiking neural network (LRRSNN). The framework integrating biological plausibility of LRRSNN with manifold learning method leverages low-rank connectivity and small-world topology to improve the efficiency and robustness of controller. To enhance training stability, we design a geometric constraint mechanism that incorporates Riemannian gradient descent. It is shown that the attitude controller based on proposed framework…

items.title: Neuromorphic self-aware wings for embodied-intelligent bionic flying microrobotics
Neuromorphic self-aware wings for embodied-intelligent bionic flying microrobotics.
items.summary: Flying insects achieve robust proprioception and agile flight control using distributed mechanoreceptors on their wings, but current bionic flying microrobots rely heavily on external sensors for state monitoring. Typical sensing solutions including offboard vision or surface-mounted devices inevitably sacrifice either flight autonomy or payload capacity. Inspired by insect wing mechanoreception, we introduce an embodied neuromorphic self-sensing paradigm that eliminates this tradeoff by enabling intrinsic, aerodynamics-maintenance proprioception in flapping-wing systems. Instead of treating the wing solely as a propulsive structure, we reengineer it into a self-contained sensory organ…

items.title: An all-magnonic neuron with tunable fading memory.
items.summary: Magnonics offers nanometer-scale wave propagation and strong nonlinearities, making it attractive for neuromorphic applications such as artificial neurons. Yet, magnonic elements with interconnections solely within the magnonic system remain challenging, preventing the realization of interconnected magnonic neurons to date. Here, we experimentally demonstrate an all-magnonic neuron that reacts to magnon inputs with thresholded, amplified magnon firing and subsequent self-reset, enabling all-magnonic operation and cascading. Our approach is based on micro-antenna excitation on an ultralow damping garnet with perpendicular magnetic anisotropy, where we exploit the positive magnon frequency…

items.title: Monolayer h-BN RF Switch Toward Monolithic Inductor Switching in Wide-Tuning-Range LC-VCOs.
items.summary: Next-generation wireless systems demand monolithic three-dimensional (3D) system-on-chip architectures to overcome planar scaling limits and reduce interconnect delays. Realizing this back-end-of-line (BEOL) integration on complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor (CMOS) platforms requires ultracompact, high-performance radio-frequency (RF) switches. Here, we present a non-volatile RF switch based on a monolayer hexagonal boron nitride (h-BN) memristor employing an Ag/h-BN/Ag structure. The device exhibits a low SET voltage of 1.11 V and stable endurance exceeding 500 cycles. items.title: Growth-Spiral Control of Defect Topology and Local Vertical Piezoresponse in Bi4Ti3O12 Thin Films.
items.summary: Aurivillius phase materials are layered ferroelectrics with high thermal stability (>600 °C) and fatigue resistance, yet their polarization is predominantly in-plane, limiting integration into vertical device architectures relevant to future memory, data storage, and neuromorphic computing concepts. Achieving robust vertical polarization in these systems remains fundamentally challenging because of crystallographic symmetry constraints. Although defects can locally reorient polarization, deterministic control of defect topology through growth-mode engineering remains largely unexplored in layered ferroelectrics. items.title: Hyphal differentiation and cell wall remodeling in Trametes versicolor underlie a layered architecture in pure mycelium materials
items.summary: Background: Pure mycelium materials grown at the air-liquid interface are promising leather alternatives, yet they are generally treated as homogeneous sheets of fungal biomass. Because basidiomycetes differentiate their hyphae into generative, skeletal and ligative cell types, the properties of such materials may instead arise from an internal tissue organisation. In this study, cell types produced by the trimitic white-rot fungus Trametes versicolor during Liquid State Surface Fermentation were characterized and the impact of their spatial organisation, mechanics and cell wall composition on the resulting material was analysed. items.title: A high-performance self-rectifying memristor for reliable neuromorphic plasticity and long-distance AM signal modulation/demodulation.
items.summary: As an innovative approach for addressing the parasitic current issue in large-scale integrated circuits, self-rectifying memristors eliminate the need for extra external circuitry, which not only significantly cuts down on manufacturing costs but also paves the way for advancing high-density integration technology. Herein, Cu2ZnSnS4 (CZTS) is innovatively introduced as the resistive switching material, and a synaptic memristor with excellent self-rectifying characteristics is successfully developed. items.title: LoopROS: A Deployable Embodied Recursive Self-Improvement Framework Based on Logical and Physical Constraints
items.summary: Embodied recursive self-improvement (RSI) endows robots with the capacity to progressively refine manipulation skills through real-world physical interaction, representing a cornerstone toward generalpurpose embodied intelligence. Yet existing embodied RSI frameworks largely remain simulationbound: they fail to realize closed-loop RSI when transferred onto uncalibrated real-world robots. This paper presents LoopROS, a deployable RSI framework built upon a constraints-as-policy principle for embodied robot. items.title: From Recursive Self-Improvement to Human-AI Reciprocal Improvement
items.summary: Recursive self-improvement advances most readily in domains where results can be verified reliably, such as mathematics and coding. Beyond these domains, progress slows as reliable signals for evaluating and guiding improvement become harder to obtain, resulting in a jagged frontier of AI capabilities. Yet even where AI self-improves autonomously, its growing capabilities do not necessarily translate into greater human ability to understand, use and build upon its outputs, challenging both continued human participation and effective oversight. We argue that recursive progress should therefore also encompass the growth of human capabilities. We propose Recursive Reciprocal Improvement (RRI)…

items.title: Multiobjective exploration of intramolecular torsional space.
items.summary: We present an exploration-first strategy for intramolecular conformational search. Because practical quantum-chemical (QC) models are approximate, candidate retention combines energy and interaction descriptors as separate objectives, while structural diversity is preserved until post-search reduction. The SEEKER (Structural Ensemble Exploration through Knowledge-Guided Evaluation and Routing) program explores explicitly declared acyclic torsions through unit-quaternion rotations while retaining fixed ring families. items.title: A Survey on Recursive Self-Improvement in Healthcare AI Agents
items.summary: Advances in persistent memory, reusable skills and adaptive training are making recursive self-improvement (RSI) increasingly relevant to healthcare agents. RSI concerns changes to the procedures that generate future improvements. This survey connects these developments with healthcare evidence by distinguishing component updates, training-generator changes and revisions of improvement procedures. We examine applications in diagnosis, reporting and question answering, together with challenges in evaluation, reliability, privacy and update governance.
